candidates.title: Operando isotope-sensitive IR for TEA versus TEOA
candidates.purpose: Test whether donor identity changes reaction-state IR features consistent with CO2-associated or hydrogen-involving species in the P01 Co-bpy context, using symmetric isotope and negative controls so any TEA-versus-TEOA difference is bounded in both donor conditions rather than inferred from products alone.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV080 and GX008 support operando IR with isotope and negative controls as a transferable strategy. EV031 and EV029 motivate the narrower proposal that donor identity can alter intermediate populations or CO2-associated adduct chemistry, but they do not establish the same species in Co-bpy. This revised card therefore compares TEA and TEOA under matched conditions and applies parallel assignment controls on both donor sides where feasible.

groups.description: Baseline operando run with TEOA under CO2 and light in the selected P01 formulation.

comparisons.inference: Reproducible donor-dependent differences in reaction-state bands under matched conditions support a donor-linked change in the reacting ensemble, but alone do not separate CO2 adduct effects from altered cobalt state or other medium effects.
Band shifts that track 13CO2 under TEOA support assignment of those bands to CO2-derived species in that donor condition; absence of shift argues against that assignment for those specific bands.
Band shifts that track 13CO2 under TEA support assignment of those bands to CO2-derived species in that donor condition; absence of shift argues against that assignment for those specific bands.
Band shifts upon H2O to D2O substitution under TEOA support involvement of exchangeable hydrogen in the assigned feature; no shift argues against that specific hydrogen-involving assignment.
Band shifts upon H2O to D2O substitution under TEA support involvement of exchangeable hydrogen in the assigned feature; no shift argues against that specific hydrogen-involving assignment.

Features present only when cobalt is included under TEOA are more consistent with cobalt-associated reaction-state species; shared features indicate donor or background contributions and limit assignment.

Features present only when cobalt is included under TEA are more consistent with cobalt-associated reaction-state species; shared features indicate donor or background contributions and limit assignment.

procedure: Verify an IR-compatible reaction cell and establish stable pre-illumination baselines for the complete P01 medium with TEA and with TEOA, using the same optical path and gas handling across all groups.
Run matched illuminated operando or near-operando CO2 experiments for TEA and TEOA, including corresponding cobalt-absent references, with identical acquisition timing and reactor configuration.

After donor-comparison reproducibility is confirmed, repeat each donor condition with 13CO2 and, where spectral quality and formulation stability remain acceptable, with D2O substitution of the aqueous component.
Process spectra against pre-illumination and component-matched references, then compare donor-dependent band emergence, isotope shifts, persistence, and decay across the paired TEA and TEOA datasets.

Relate any donor-dependent spectral differences to separately measured matched catalytic outputs only descriptively, avoiding unique structural or pathway claims unless isotope and control behavior are internally consistent on both donor sides.
measurements: Time-resolved IR spectra under illumination for all groups.
Wavenumber positions, isotope shifts, and temporal evolution of donor-dependent bands under TEA and TEOA.
Presence or absence of candidate bands in cobalt-present versus cobalt-absent references for each donor.
Symmetry of 13CO2 and D2O assignment behavior across TEA and TEOA conditions.
Signal-to-noise, baseline stability, repeatability across replicate runs, and degree of band overlap.
candidates.supports: Support for H05 would be a reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in reaction-state IR features under otherwise matched conditions, with at least one donor-dependent feature showing internally consistent isotope behavior and cobalt dependence on the relevant donor side. The strongest support is when analogous assignment controls bound TEA and TEOA features differently, consistent with donor-specific CO2-associated or hydrogen-involving chemistry rather than simple background differences.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H05 would be that TEA and TEOA show no reproducible donor-dependent reaction-state IR differences beyond baseline noise or generic medium changes, or that apparent differences disappear once symmetric isotope and cobalt-absent controls are applied. That outcome would favor explanations centered elsewhere, such as quenching kinetics, cobalt-state changes not resolved here, or uncontrolled catalytic variability.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if spectra are dominated by overlap, weak signals, or baseline drift; if D2O or 13CO2 causes broad perturbation without interpretable assignment value; if only one donor condition yields usable isotope-control data; or if donor-dependent bands cannot be separated from cobalt-free backgrounds. In that case the experiment remains descriptive and cannot cleanly discriminate H05 from competing explanations.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent literature conditions. Use the source-verified P01 formulation where available; otherwise first pilot each donor condition separately to find the highest concentration, path length, and collection time that preserve unsaturated absorbance and stable baselines. Keep reactor geometry, illumination, gas handling, and acquisition timing identical across TEA and TEOA. Apply 13CO2 and D2O only after the corresponding unlabeled donor condition gives reproducible transient bands. If D2O destabilizes one donor formulation or causes severe rate collapse, retain that arm as a bounded assignment aid and narrow inference accordingly rather than treating TEA and TEOA as fully matched.
candidates.limitations: Evidence is transferred from non-Co systems and general methods. Band assignment may remain ambiguous because donor, solvent, bicarbonate or carbonate, products, and cobalt-ligand features can overlap. Isotope substitution can alter kinetics as well as frequencies. Near-operando spectra may miss the true operating state, and operando IR alone cannot prove the primary quenching route, exact adduct identity, or whether a detected species is on-path rather than spectator. Cobalt-absent controls bound background contributions but do not separately isolate all non-cobalt components.
